cards.explanation: The answer is that the LORD will allure her and speak to her tenderly. He says, "…I will allure her and lead her to the wilderness, and speak to her tenderly." After all that hard talk, I was ready for a slammed door, friends. Instead the next thing out of His mouth is a soft voice, and I had to read it twice.

The answer is vineyards. Earlier the LORD talked about taking things away (Hosea 2:9-12). Now, in the wilderness, He says, "There I will give back her vineyards…" Taking is one thing, friends, but giving back is a whole different promise.

The answer is hope. Achor is where Achan was stoned (Joshua 7:24-26), after he took things he was told not to take (Joshua 7:1; 7:20-21). And the LORD says He will make that same valley "…into a gateway of hope." He takes a place with a heavy name and gives it a brand new label, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "There she will respond as she did in the days of her youth, as in the day she came up out of Egypt." He points back to the day she left Egypt and says she'll answer Him that way again. I think that's a sweet memory to hand somebody, bakers.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "you will call Me ‘my Husband,’ and no longer call Me ‘my Master.’" The card had the two names swapped around, friends. It's Husband that they'll say, and Master that they won't.

The answer is the names of the Baals. The LORD says, "…I will remove from her lips the names of the Baals; no longer will their names be invoked." The Baals were false gods her lips had been calling on, friends. He says He'll take those names right out of her mouth.

The answer is the beasts and birds and crawling creatures. That's the surprise guest list, friends! The LORD says, "…I will make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air and the creatures that crawl on the ground." Animals are named right alongside the promise. I'd be shocked too, and I once got startled by my own mustache.

The answer is bow and sword and battle. The LORD says, "…I will abolish bow and sword and battle in the land…" The weapons go, friends, and the fighting goes with them. It's the kind of cleanup I'd happily volunteer for.

The answer is True. After abolishing bow and sword and battle, the LORD says, "…and will make them lie down in safety." Picture lying down with the fighting gone from the land, bakers. I haven't rested that easy since my days on a nice flat counter.
The answer is False. The LORD says, "So I will betroth you to Me forever…" No season in that word, friends. Forever means forever, and that's why this one is false.

The answer is that they will come to know the LORD. The LORD says, "And I will betroth you in faithfulness, and you will know the LORD." The betrothal and the knowing are right next to each other, friends. I think there's something good in that pairing.

The answer is grain. The LORD says, "And the earth will respond to the grain, to the new wine and oil…" It's a whole chain, friends: heavens, earth, then grain, wine and oil. I'd love a chain of command in my bakery that smooth.
The answer is True. The LORD says, "…I will have compassion on ‘No Compassion.’…" The very name that said no compassion gets compassion, friends. I like how that name takes a turn.

The answer is "You are My people." The LORD says, "I will say to those called 'Not My People,' 'You are My people.'" The name said one thing and He says the opposite, friends. I'd frame that sentence if I had a wall.

The answer is "You are my God." The LORD says, "You are My people…" and then they say, "You are my God." He speaks first, and they answer Him back, friends. It's the last line of the passage and it's a good one to end on.
